$comment: ADR-362: in-game guide content. Sections are data-driven: prose ({ text } / intro / label) carries NO digits — every number a player reads is a { fact, label, format } entry resolved by src/guide.ts from the same data files and named constants the game reads. Icon references are keys only (item / piece / vehicle / mount / pet); ADR-364 wires the art. Controls rows ({ keys }) are pinned to packages/input/profiles/keyboardMouse.json by the ADR-362 tests, except the character-sheet row, which is pinned to the menu hotkey in apps/client/src/game-menus.ts. Image rows ({ image, caption }) are composed in apps/client/src/task364-art.ts from the game's own sprites and runtime-painted art; captions carry no digits either.

sections.intro: You wake up in a wild valley with empty hands. Gather, craft, build a shelter, and stay fed, warm and dry.

items.text: Gather sticks, logs, stone and fibre from the world around you with your bare hands or a tool.
Your pack holds what you carry; the hotbar holds what you can use at once. Eat and drink before your vitals run low.
Plant a claim flag before you build, or your walls belong to no one and anyone can take them down.
When night falls, zombies grow bold. Light and walls keep you alive until dawn.

sections.title: Getting started

sections.intro: Default keyboard and mouse controls. Gamepad and touch use the same actions with their own prompts.

items.label: Hold to open the radial menu
Raise terrain with a shovel in hand
Lower terrain with a shovel in hand

items.text: On a gamepad the same actions live on sticks, triggers and buttons; on touch, on-screen buttons.
Hold the attack button to charge a heavy swing.

sections.title: Controls

sections.intro: What the pictures on your screen mean. The same icons appear in the HUD, the character sheet and menus.

items.text: Health, hunger, thirst and stamina sit on the HUD. When one runs low, eat, drink or rest before it starts draining health.
The temperature gauge shows how warm your body feels, not the air. Cold and heat warnings appear before damage does.

items.label: Body temperature where freezing damage starts
Body temperature where overheating damage starts

items.text: Wetness shows as damp, wet, then soaked. Soaked clothing insulates far less than dry clothing.
Disease chips on the HUD name what ails you and how long it has left. Open the character sheet for timers and cures.
The compass points north and settles when you stop turning. Map markers show your party, your clan and your own pins.
Every item, crop and creature in this guide shows its own icon. If a picture is missing, the guide still names the thing.

sections.title: Icons

sections.intro: Sickness comes from risky food and drink, wounds, cold, heat and other sick people. Most diseases pass on their own or with a cure.

items.text: Raw meat, untreated water, rotten food and sick food can all make you ill. Cook food and boil water first.
A cloth mask blocks catching a cold or the flu from someone close by.

items.label: Close contact that can spread illness
Cold exposure before a cold can take hold
Heat exposure before heatstroke can take hold
Care cure for a cold or the flu: stay dry, fed, hydrated and warm without a break
An untreated cold turns into the flu after

items.text: Death clears every disease, infection and wetness. You wake up clean, but your body stays where it fell.

sections.title: Diseases

sections.intro: Your body cools and warms with the air, the rain, your clothes and nearby fire. Shelter and insulation keep the cold off.

items.text: Wet clothing loses much of its insulation. Dry off by a fire or under a roof.

items.label: Insulation lost when clothing is soaked

items.text: A fire warms only the room it burns in. Walls and a roof hold the heat; a fire outside warms no one inside.

items.label: Most a fire can warm its room
Time for a room to feel most of a fire's warmth
Water freezes and food stops spoiling at or below

items.text: Body temperature warnings come in stages: chilly, cold, freezing on the cold side, and hot, sweltering, overheating on the warm side. Only the worst stage on each side harms you.
Standing in water soaks you faster than any rain. Wading is a quick way to get wet.

sections.title: Temperature

sections.intro: Cooking turns raw food into safe meals. A lit campfire is your first kitchen; better stations unlock better recipes.

items.text: Fired stations must be lit to cook. A wood stove cooks like a campfire and also warms its room.
A held torch can boil water and cook meat in a pinch.
Food spoils in stages, and spoiled food feeds you less and can sicken you.
Salt keeps food fresh longer in a salt barrel, a curing box or a cold store. Salt is spent while food is stored and spoilable.

items.label: Food stops spoiling at or below

items.text: Honey Tea cures a cold and the flu. Keep some brewed before winter.

sections.title: Cooking

sections.intro: Claim land first, then build on it. Walls, floors, roofs, doors and furniture snap to a grid; higher floors need support below.

items.caption: The green hologram shows where the piece will stand

items.text: A claim flag marks land as yours. Only you and your clan may build, repair or open containers inside it.

items.caption: A claim flag and a clan flag mark land as yours

items.label: Wait after damage before a repair
Materials returned when you demolish your own build

items.text: Upper decks must connect to walls below. A deck with no support collapses.
Doors can be locked to your clan. A broken clan gate stands open until it is repaired.
Paint a piece with dye and a paint brush to make it yours.

sections.title: Building

sections.intro: AI humans live in the world with their own wants. Walk up to one and offer what they ask for, and they will work for you.

items.text: Each AI human wants one fixed item. Hand it over and they join you; the item leaves your pack the moment they are hired.

items.label: Different items AI humans may ask for

items.text: Give a hired worker a job: Gather, Farm, Defend, Craft or Maintain. They keep working while you are away and across saves.
Hired workers furnish and upgrade their homes, garden, tame livestock, fill troughs and refuel lit fires.
When idle, AI humans live their own lives: they travel, keep mounts, settle ruins and defend their homes.

items.label: A journey counts as long beyond
Turrets an AI home defence may build
Barbed wire an AI home defence may build
Safe ground around spawn points, beds and AI homes

items.text: A host can turn new AI humans off. Workers already hired keep working.

sections.title: AI humans

sections.intro: Tame pets with their favourite treats, keep farm animals fed, and they will guard, produce and follow.

items.text: Pets have their own skill trees and grow stronger as they gain levels. Each species loves some treats and hates others.

items.caption: Offer a Labrador its favourite treat

items.text: Farm animals eat hay from troughs and graze grass. A full trough keeps them fed while you are away.

items.caption: Keep the trough filled so farm animals stay fed

items.label: One feeding keeps a mount fed for

items.text: Lead an animal with a rope. Tame animals stay calm and do not attack on sight.
Dung fertilises crops longer than ordinary fertiliser, then vanishes quickly if left on the ground.

items.label: Dung left on the ground lasts
Dung each animal drops per day

sections.title: Tamed and farmed animals

sections.intro: Tame a mount, saddle it, and ride. Harness a mount to pull wagons, carts, carriages and a chariot.

items.text: Feed a mount its liked food to tame it. A tame mount stays yours until it dies.

items.label: Saddlebags by saddle tier, leather to steel

items.text: Saddles are crafted at a workbench and carry bags. Better saddles hold more.

items.label: Hook a mount to a drawn vehicle with a

items.text: Ride in the driver's seat to steer the pulling mount yourself. The mount's own rider always steers first.

sections.title: Mounts and vehicles

sections.intro: Till soil with a hoe, plant seeds, water and fertilise. Seeds come only from gathering the wild plant of the same crop.

items.label: Slowest crops, the trees, mature in about

items.text: Crops need tilled soil, water and light. Rain waters for you; a watering can does the rest.
Crops sleep through the last day of fall and all of winter, and wake in spring.

items.label: Dormant days at the end of fall

items.text: Fruit trees die in a hard frost, but ordinary trees and berry bushes survive it.

sections.title: Crops and farming

sections.intro: Store each resource where it belongs. The right store keeps the right goods, and salt stores keep food fresh.

items.label: Different crops a crop store holds

items.text: Log, stick and stone stores each take only their own kind. Seeds stay in ordinary storage, not the crop store.

items.label: Slots in an ordinary storage box

items.text: Salt stores slow spoilage while they hold salt. Better stores slow it more.
When you die, your things drop in a death bag where you fell. Only you may open it at first.

items.label: Only you may open your death bag for

sections.title: Storage

sections.intro: Four seasons turn the year. Weather follows the season, and so do temperature, snow and crops.

items.text: Rain wets you and cools the air. Storms wet you faster and chill you more. Snow wets you slowly but freezes the ground.

sections.title: Seasons and weather

sections.intro: Zombies hunt at night and answer noise. Build walls, spike barricades and turrets, and keep a safe radius around home.

items.text: Zombies are calm by day and aggressive from dusk to dawn. Hordes are always aggressive.

items.label: Zombies expected each minute at night, per player

items.text: Noise draws zombies: gathering, building, fighting and doors all make it.

items.label: Safe ground around spawn points, beds and AI homes

items.text: Hordes ignore safe ground. Everything else stays out of it.
Fire spreads between twig and wood pieces, and rain puts it out.

items.label: Chance fire spreads to a neighbour each check

sections.intro: Trade with other players, join a clan, and share claims. There are no shopkeepers: every stall is another player's.

items.text: Set up a stall, stock it, name it and set prices in any item. Coin is the usual currency.

items.label: Most characters in a stall name

items.text: A destroyed stall spills its stock and till on the ground for anyone to take.
Clan stalls follow clan ranks: leaders and officers manage them, members stock them, and anyone may buy while they are open.
Guests arriving by friend code spawn near the host, inside safe ground.
